newsitem.title: UK: Dollar/yen volatilities soften as spot steadies.
newsitem.headline: Dollar/yen volatilities soften as spot steadies.

text.p: Implied volatilities for dollar/yen options eased across the board as the dollar cooled off against the yen in the spot market, trading near its session high but steering clear of the 127-yen level.

There was little inspiration for options trading today amid a lack of fresh factors, with milder-than-expected inflation data out of the UK failing to have much impact on sterling volatilities, traders said.
"Yen volatilities are off a bit because of the spot market, but that's about it. There's been some dollar/mark traded at the longer end but nothing major," said one U.S. bank trader here.
One-month dollar/yen volatilities were at 9.30/9.80 percent at 1110 GMT, down from 9.70/10.00 in late European trade on Friday. One-year vols softened to 10.40/10.60 from 10.50/10.70.
One-month dollar/mark vols edged down to 8.90/9.20 percent from Friday's 9.00/9.30, while one-year was steady.
Spot sterling's rise to a fresh 4-1/2-year high of 2.8052 marks overnight had little impact on options, traders said.
Volatilities also shrugged off benign UK inflation data today, which dampened perceptions of a sharp rise in interest rates in the near future, they added.
One-month sterling/mark volatilities were quoted at 9.45/9.85 percent against Friday's 9.50/9.90, while cable vols eased to 7.45/7.75 percent from Friday's 7.70/8.00.
Risk reversals for dollar/mark favoured mark puts at 0.15/0.35 percent against Friday's 0.0/0.2, while dollar/yen risk reversals were bid for yen puts at 0.2/0.5 versus 0.3/0.6, traders said.
